claims.text: Post-deformation annealing can induce full recrystallization and grain refinement in HfZrTiTa0.53.
The annealing-induced microstructure will improve tensile ductility and uniform elongation in HfZrTiTa0.53.
The proposed ductility improvement will occur without sacrificing the high strength of HfZrTiTa0.53.
The proposed treatment will preserve impact-triggered energy release in HfZrTiTa0.53.
Untreated HfZrTiTa0.53 has a yield strength of approximately 786 MPa.
Untreated HfZrTiTa0.53 has a compressive strength of approximately 1314 MPa.
Untreated HfZrTiTa0.53 has approximately 13.5% total elongation.
The as-processed HfZrTiTa0.53 likely has a relatively coarse or heterogeneous microstructure.
A tailored annealing treatment will produce a homogeneous fine-grained microstructure in HfZrTiTa0.53.
The annealed HfZrTiTa0.53 microstructure will be single phase.
Grain refinement increases grain-boundary density and promotes more uniform dislocation activity and strain hardening.
More homogeneous plastic flow and sustained dislocation interactions increase uniform elongation.
A fully recrystallized fine-grained CoCrNiV alloy exhibits high strength and enhanced ductility through stable strain hardening involving dislocations and stacking faults.
Controlled precipitate engineering can produce simultaneous high strength and high uniform elongation in a multi-principal-element alloy.
Annealing will raise tensile uniform elongation in HfZrTiTa0.53 to approximately 20–25%.
Annealed HfZrTiTa0.53 will retain a yield strength of at least 786 MPa.
The beneficial effect is expected at room temperature and a tensile strain rate around 10^-3 s^-1.
Nonoptimal annealing temperature, time, or processing sequence may reduce tensile ductility or impact performance.

contradictions.description: The 13.5% baseline is characterized as total elongation or merely elongation, but the prediction implicitly treats it as a tensile uniform-elongation baseline. Total, terminal, and uniform elongation are not interchangeable metrics.

The hypothesis limits the expected effect to a quasi-static strain rate near 10^-3 s^-1 while also requiring impact-energy preservation; no high-rate impact regime or strain-rate limit is specified, so the claimed matched conditions cannot apply literally to both quasi-static tensile and impact loading.
